newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt futures rally, end sharply higher.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt futures rally, end sharply higher.

text.p: U.S. debt futures posted sharp gains on a bullish mix of short-term technicals and fundamentals.
U.S. March T-bond futures surged more than a point to post a session high at 111-15/32, fueled by December economic data that showed moderate growth with minimal inflation, traders said.

After steep losses on Friday and lethargy on Monday, traders said many players covered their short positions after the data, with technical buying aiding gains. Traders noted buy stops in March above 111-000 and above 111-8/32.
Still, some noted that Tuesday's action was within Friday's range.
In technical terms, that's an inside day on daily bar charts and can be considered a corrective move.
"It throws things back into a level of confusion," a Treasury notes trader said. "It was a constructive day, but there's nothing great on the upside," he said.

Early in the day, U.S. December consumer price and retail sales data set the tone. Retail sales rose 0.6 percent overall and ex-autos, and consumer prices rose 0.3 percent and 0.1 percent ex-food and energy.
U.S. November retail sales were revised up to minus 0.2 percent from minus 0.4 percent. Retail sales in November excluding autos were revised down to unchanged from up 0.3 percent.

"I think this data shows inflation isn't a problem and there's a little bit of growth going on," a Eurodollar trader said. "I think the Fed won't want to choke off growth if there are few signs of inflation," he added.
He said the data dampened prospects for an interest rate hike in February.
In the short-end, traders said short-covering and mild technical strength were primary drivers for the rally.
June takes over lead contract status from March on Wednesday, with resistance seen at 94.20 and 94.23-24. Support was pegged at 94.15.

At settlement, March T-bonds were up 1-00 to 111-13/32, T-notes rose 19/32 to 108-17/32, muni-bonds gained 26/32 to 115-2/32, T-bills rose two basis points to 94.90, and March Eurodollars rose three basis points to 94.36. ((DerivativesDesk(312)408-8750/E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com))
